Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our audit team is starting to assemble evidence for Finexa's Q1 procurement review and has a couple of clarifying questions about Redwood's SOC 2 Type II applicability across deployment modes. Specifically: 

1) For customers on Hosted API (multi-tenant), we assume the SOC 2 Type II report covers ALL hosted endpoints in the report period — is that correct?
2) For Dedicated pools (reserved capacity), does Redwood include those pools in the same SOC 2 report, or are they handled as a separate control boundary?
3) For Private/VPC and on-prem deployments, what evidence can Redwood provide (bridge letter, attestation, or environment-specific controls) to demonstrate continuity across the audit window?

Audit timeline: our review window is Jan 1, 2026 — Dec 31, 2026. We need confirmation about which modes are in-scope for that window and a short list of deliverables (report PDF, bridge letter, control owner contacts).

Can you please respond with the scope mapping and any templates your team prefers for evidence requests?

Appreciate it — we want to align before the SIG is due next week.

Best,
Gail Richardson
Head of Vendor Risk — Finexa Financial

Gail,

Thanks for the clear questions — copying Ben (sales ops), Kim (security/compliance), and Soojin (customer success) to help round out answers and evidence. Short answers up front, then details below.

- Hosted API: covered by Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report for the audit period (report PDF available).
- Dedicated: included in the SOC 2 report when the Dedicated pool is managed and operated by Redwood in our control plane; there are some tenant-boundary considerations for customer-managed networking.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: these are generally out-of-scope for the hosted SOC 2 report; we provide bridge letters and environment-specific attestation packages instead.

I attached a short SOC 2 summary and an evidence matrix template (hosting_evidence_matrix.xlsx) to accelerate mapping. Next steps I propose:

1) Finexa completes the matrix with the list of endpoints/workloads you expect to use (hosted/dedicated/private).
2) Our team will mark each row with the available artifact (Type II PDF, bridge letter, runbook, or customer-managed evidence).
3) We will confirm the audit window mapping against your Jan–Dec 2026 period and note any exceptions (e.g., newly onboarded Dedicated pools that came online mid-period).

Couple of clarifying notes:
- "Included" Dedicated pools: if the pool is provisioned in Redwood-managed infra and the tenant isolation is enforced by Redwood, it is typically in-scope. If the customer requested an isolated, customer-owned network appliance (on their VLAN) or we shipped a packaged on-prem instance, that footprint will usually be out-of-scope for the standard Type II.
- Bridge letters: we can provide bridge letters that reference the audit period and list the controls that are not covered by the standard report, with proposed compensating controls.

I'll put together a short mutual action plan once Finexa completes the attached matrix.

Thanks,
